cues: A librarian reassures him that everything of worth has been digitised.
He does not use a computer, and there is something irreplaceable about a physical book: its look, its smell, its heft.
Then the last memory closes the circle: in nineteen sixty seven, rummaging in the stacks, he found an eighteen seventy three book on migraine, which inspired his own first book.
Digitise the shelf, and you may keep the text.
But you lose the lucky accident.
text: A librarian reassures him that everything of worth has been digitised. He is not reassured. He does not use a computer, and there is something irreplaceable about a physical book: its look, its smell, its heft. Then the last memory closes the circle: in nineteen sixty seven, rummaging in the stacks, he found an eighteen seventy three book on migraine, which inspired his own first book. Digitise the shelf, and you may keep the text. But you lose the lucky accident.
